document_additions.title: Mercy Road Case: 2298 Review Copy
document_additions.found: Pritchard voluntarily offers his retained review copy when asked about Quill while explaining the pike route. It lies in the open on his desk after that conversation. Taking the copy records optional mq02c stage16; current possession controls docket_2298_held.
document_additions.text:
MERCY ROAD CASE: SPRING 2298
Retained review copy. Not a pardon in any current case.

The carrier's dated receipt and two sworn accounts place the condemned man away from the road at the hour alleged. Copies were entered with Magistrate Esther Quill before sentence was carried out.

I received the warrant and carried it out. I later checked the accounts against the receiving ledger. We hanged an innocent man. I have kept the rope; it is not an answer. The finding should have gone into the court record then. I am making this copy available now.

Owen Pritchard, Sheriff
Attached: entry receipt bearing E. Quill's court mark.
document_additions.constraints: No new named victim, witness actor or family connection. This records Quill's receipt before execution and Pritchard's later corroboration; it does not imply Pritchard knew before the drop. The current defendant is still entitled to a hearing, not presumed innocent because an earlier case was wrong.

journal_replacements.log: You asked Pritchard to call the fair without a road report. Talbot is posting the notice. The three roads remain open if you change your mind.
Quill adjourned after you presented the 2298 review copy. The current accused remains alive under review; this is not a pardon.

journal_replacements.set_by: Taking the review copy offered by Pritchard. Stage16 records acquisition; docket_2298_held must reflect current possession, not a permanently latched acquisition stage.
journal_replacements.log: Pritchard gave you his review of the 2298 hanging, with the court's receipt for the evidence. Quill can be asked to enter it alongside the current case.
Captain Blevins has given a final warning. Eleven people are alive below. Stop the firing or bring them up before he turns the key.
The local deadline ran out. Captain Blevins fired with the shift still below. The cage came up empty. You gave no order, but the knocking has stopped.
The delegates and local witnesses backed the Decoration Day truce. Brigg accepted a limited search instead of taking the camp-ground.
The grain barge reached Greenwater through Hangman's Chute. Some cargo was lost in the rapids.
The occupied Queen burned with the grain lashed alongside. People tried to reach the water. The cargo is lost; the crew's account still needs witnesses.

talk_replacements.text: Red Hollow, by the pike. You'll pass Brigg's gate at the gap. Ask what evidence Esther Quill has heard before you pay for a pardon. A bench on a wagon isn't proof of a fair hearing.
Gantt suspected a common purse. One road isn't the whole account. Decoration Day's in a week. I'll ask every flag in these valleys to eat my chicken and answer questions where the town can hear.

Hear that? Hoist code. Eleven alive below, my Pell among them. Captain Blevins is making ready to fire. I can work the cage. Decide whether you're starting the rescue before he gives the final warning.

button_replacements.from: I can't swear for a whole town.
button_replacements.to: What can I promise for myself?

talk_replacements.text: Delegate Belden, Commonwealth provisioning. There is a bowl if you want one. Eating here commits you to nothing.
That silver case carries a mark from case-working tools I made years ago. Not the bullet mould. Come by after dark and I'll show you the drawings; they don't tell us the customer's name.
Stand easy. Search the landing with the local officers and witnesses present. We do not take the fair tonight. I will not make a second shooting out of a public inquiry.
There's a rope below the steps. If you let them take me, they'll hang me here. You've read the book. Speak it, bargain with it, or tell them you won't stop them. At least name what you're choosing.
Granger has the rope. I know these people. I'll keep them off the steps while you decide. Leaving to think is not telling them to hang a man. If you mean that, say it where I can hear.

The road account records your share. That's why I thought you might understand the price. Here: six years of payments, and the present work in four columns. Read it before you decide what my arithmetic is worth.
Two hundred, and a berth. Tell Opal the Chute took it. Delegate Belden has a soup wagon; he'll offer a bowl. I'm selling you a share, not a promise that his pot replaces the winter grain.

Delegate Belden's wagon reached Greenwater. People ate. Now he's asking about a continuing agreement, and they can argue over it with something in their stomachs. The missing grain still belongs on somebody's account.

One cut frees the barge for the Chute. Or burn the Queen. Thirty people are aboard - crew, cooks, the fiddler - and the winter grain is still lashed alongside. Fire can take them and the cargo. Say what you're ordering.
We brought back less than we needed. Enough to stretch the pot, not enough to stop counting. We'll measure what came home before anybody calls it a victory. Thank you for what you brought.
I asked for the grain and one man's answer. Now the cargo's burned and people are missing. Don't give me a number you haven't counted. Bring the living to the planks. We'll need every hand.
You won the barge from Hatcher? Every sack? Then we'll count it home. Now tell me what you mean to do with him. I want him on the steeple, and you know what that means.

Signatory carriers vote on the charter rate. Nell Fenwick voted against me twice and for me once. Other carriers want independent rates. Leaving a voluntary agreement mustn't cost them the right to use the road.

The small carriers ask that too. One bad season can sell them to people in my own Compact who smile just the way I do. I know it. I haven't a rule for it yet. I'd sooner admit that than sell you a pig in a sack.
Juno Three-Fords. I carried this through three fords without opening it. Find me Sheriff Pritchard, then find me a dry bench. In that order.
Help on the Tellico! Penny a sheet, patrons of letters. The stranger's reasons cost extra, and I don't have them.
News from the Tellico, and three tellings for every tale. Penny a sheet. If you want a witness, don't mistake the printer for one.
News from the Tellico, and three tellings for every tale. Penny a sheet. If you want a witness, don't mistake the printer for one.
A share on the road, a bargain on the page. Penny a sheet. I print the price I'm told; I wasn't there to call it fair.

betrayal_ballad.title: The Stranger and the Tellico Road
betrayal_ballad.found: Granger's sheet for outcome exploited with method betrayal. The trade sheet is restricted to method deal.
betrayal_ballad.text:
THE STRANGER AND THE TELLICO ROAD
A new ballad. T. Granger, printer. One penny.
Set from accounts heard in Mercy Crossing.

Come gather, valley people, where the road comes down the grade;
I'll sell the news I've gathered, and the rhymes that I have made.
A train came off at Tellico. A stranger reached our town.
The rest depends on who you ask, and what they won't set down.

One tells it over supper; one swears the telling's wrong.
I've ink enough for either, but there's only room for song.
I did not ride that morning or stand beside the load.
I set what folk have told me of the strangers on the road.

The talk is trouble on the road; the telling turns to blame.
Each teller sets the reckoning beside a different name.
I wasn't there to count the cost or judge what passed that day.
The ink is mine; the deeds are not. Hear what the witnesses say.
